title: Fixed-object sifted homotopy-colimit criterion for simplicial categories
statement: Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences, object-preserving locally Kan replacement and the derived coherent nerve $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and spaces, coherent diagrams and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $X$, write $\langle X\rangle$ for its homotopy type, namely the space represented by a Kan replacement for the weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Fix a small set $O$, a small ordinary category $J$, and a strict functor $C_\bullet:J\to\mathrm{sCat}$ whose values have object set exactly $O$ and whose structure functors are the identity on $O$. Let $C$ be another simplicial category with object set $O$, and let $u_j:C_j\to C$ be a strictly compatible cocone, identity on $O$. Suppose $N(J)$ is sifted, meaning that its indexed colimits in spaces exist and commute with finite products. Suppose that for every $x,y\in O$ the induced coherent cocone exhibits $\langle C(x,y)\rangle$ as the colimit of $j\mapsto\langle C_j(x,y)\rangle$ in spaces. Then the cocone induced by $u_\bullet$ exhibits $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(C)$ as the colimit of $j\mapsto\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(C_j)$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. In particular the assertion identifies the specified cocone, not merely its apex up to an unspecified equivalence; it is natural in maps of such cocones. All sets and diagrams fit in fixed universes, enlarged when necessary.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.10, printed pp.111-112, and the homotopy-theory identification in lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopical result.

proof.text: Apply the functorial object-preserving locally Kan replacement $A\to RA$ to the entire diagram and cocone. Its naturality makes $RC_j\to RC$ a strictly compatible cocone, still identity on $O$. Every $C_j(x,y)\to RC_j(x,y)$ and $C(x,y)\to RC(x,y)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, so the assumed colimiting mapping-space cocones remain colimiting after these natural identifications. The derived coherent nerves in the conclusion are exactly $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RC_j)$ and $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RC)$ by the definition $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)$ in the cited comparison theorem. We work with these locally Kan categories from now on.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.10, pp.111-112; agent Segal-space proof of its mapping-space criterion

proof.text: Form the enriched Segal nerves $B(RC_j)$ and $B(RC)$ of the cited realization theorem. Their degree-$n$ spaces are coproducts indexed by the same discrete set $O^{n+1}$, with summands the products of the $n$ mapping spaces. This includes degree zero, where each summand is the point. Since all structure functors and all cocone legs are identity on $O$, none of these maps mixes the summand labels. Thus in each degree the specified cocone is the coproduct over fixed tuples of the specified product cocones.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.10, pp.111-112; agent Segal-space proof of its mapping-space criterion

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq0$ and a tuple $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\in O^{n+1}$. The hypothesis that $N(J)$-colimits in spaces commute with finite products applies to the $n$ mapping-space diagrams $j\mapsto\langle RC_j(x_{r-1},x_r)\rangle$. By the mapping-space colimit hypothesis and Step 1, its canonical comparison gives
$$\operatorname{colim}_{j\in N(J)}\prod_{r=1}^n\langle RC_j(x_{r-1},x_r)\rangle\simeq\prod_{r=1}^n\langle RC(x_{r-1},x_r)\rangle.$$
It is precisely the map induced by the products of the given cocone legs. For $n=0$ this is the empty-product part of siftedness: the constant point cocone has colimit a point. No assertion about arbitrary pullbacks or complete-Segal object spaces is used.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.10, pp.111-112; agent Segal-space proof of its mapping-space criterion

proof.text:
Write $I=O^{n+1}$, $P_{j,t}=\prod_{r=1}^n\langle RC_j(x_{r-1},x_r)\rangle$ and $P_t=\prod_{r=1}^n\langle RC(x_{r-1},x_r)\rangle$ for $t=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\in I$. For a diagram $F$ of spaces let $\operatorname{Coc}(F,T)$ be the space of coherent transformations $F\to\Delta T$. For every test space $T$, Step 3 and the dual mapping-space criterion of the cited cocone-calculus lemma give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}\!\left(\coprod_{t\in I}P_t,T\right)\simeq\prod_{t\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(P_t,T)\simeq\prod_{t\in I}\operatorname{Coc}(P_{\bullet,t},T)\simeq\operatorname{Coc}\!\left(\coprod_{t\in I}P_{\bullet,t},T\right).$$
Here $\mathcal S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan})$ as in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and all diagrams $P_{\bullet,t}$ and $\coprod_tP_{\bullet,t}$ are strict functors $J\to\mathbf{Kan}$ regarded as coherent diagrams. The first equivalence holds because the coherent-nerve comparison identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X,T)$ naturally with the Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}(X,T)$, and $\operatorname{Fun}(\coprod_tP_t,T)=\prod_t\operatorname{Fun}(P_t,T)$ as simplicial sets. For the last equivalence, an $m$-simplex of the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Coc}(F,T)$ is a map $N(J)\times\Delta^{m+1}\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan})$, that is a simplicial functor $\mathfrak C[N(J)\times\Delta^{m+1}]\to\mathbf{Kan}$, which is degenerate at $F$ on $N(J)\times\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,m\}}$ and constant at $T$ on $N(J)\times\{m+1\}$. Its remaining data are simplicial maps from the mapping simplicial sets of $\mathfrak C[N(J)\times\Delta^{m+1}]$ into $\operatorname{Fun}(F(j),T)$, compatible with composition. For $F=\coprod_tP_{\bullet,t}$ the target is $\prod_t\operatorname{Fun}(P_{j,t},T)$, the source-side composites act by the strict structure maps of $F$, which carry the $t$-th summand to the $t$-th summand, and the target side is the identity of $T$; so restricting to each summand and assembling by disjoint union are inverse bijections in every simplicial degree, compatible with the operators. This is the displayed isomorphism, on maps, homotopies and every higher compatibility. These operations respect structure maps because all of them preserve the tuple labels. The composite is the comparison induced by the actual coproduct cocone legs, since its $t$th component is precomposition with the corresponding product leg of Step 3. For $I=\varnothing$, both sides are the point and the same comparison applies. The cocone-calculus criterion therefore makes $\coprod_tP_{j,t}\to\coprod_tP_t$ colimiting. Thus $B(RC_j)\to B(RC)$ is colimiting in every degree. The pointwise-colimit assertion of the realization theorem makes it a colimit cocone in $\mathcal P_\Delta$.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.10, pp.111-112; agent Segal-space proof of its mapping-space criterion

proof.text:
Apply $\mathfrak L$ to the colimiting cocone of Step 4; the realization theorem says its image is colimiting in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The coherent natural equivalence $\vartheta$ gives a map of this entire cocone to the cocone $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(RC_j)\to\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(RC)$, with equivalence components $\vartheta_{RC_j}$ and $\vartheta_{RC}$. This retains all legs and higher compatibility homotopies.

To identify the original specified cocone, write $\eta_A:A\to RA$ for the natural replacement map. It is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence: its mapping-set maps are weak equivalences and it fixes objects. The homotopy-theory identification of the coherent-nerve comparison therefore makes $e_A=\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(\eta_A):\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)\to\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)$ an equivalence. For every original leg $u_j:C_j\to C$, naturality gives $\eta_Cu_j=R(u_j)\eta_{C_j}$, hence
$$e_C\,\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(u_j)\simeq\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(R(u_j))\,e_{C_j}.$$
The same equality holds for all structure maps and their composites, so $e$ is an equivalence of the original specified cocone with the twice-replaced one. The cited functor-calculus criterion makes these componentwise equivalences equivalences of coherent diagrams and cocones. Such an equivalence preserves the colimit property, because it identifies the mapping spaces to every test cocone and hence the condition of being initial. Thus the original cocone with apex $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(C)$ is colimiting. All displayed comparison maps are natural in maps of the original cocones, which proves the required naturality.
